Partition tools are scary because you see the result only
once it is written. Equinox draws the disk twice: as it is,
and as the plan will leave it.
Every action, from resize to format, joins the plan first.
Mounted partitions and the EFI partition you booted from are

Each step checks the filesystem first, saves the table and
writes it last, so a failure leaves the old layout.
Equinox uses the disk code Sunrise installs with, through a
typed service, and lists the shell command behind each step.
It reads without root and asks for authentication only when

Requires: a typed disk service for clients, ext2 shrink and grow, a disk command for the shell, and a way to run a plan from the live system. Today Zenith formats and checks ext2 and FAT32, and only Sunrise writes partitions. Values are illustrative.
